decisions.location: Introduction, p. 301 (see also Table 2 and pp. 308–310)
decisions.quote:
Replication of Professor Imai’s (2005) analysis reveals
a series of errors that call into question the magnitude,
significance, and robustness of his matching estimates.
decisions.reason: Under the codebook rules for earlier replication/reanalysis attempts, an earlier reanalysis is a target when the current paper directly re-tests its findings. Gerber and Green (2005) empirically re-runs Imai (2005)'s propensity score matching computer program on the exact dataset version that Imai analyzed (Table 2, pp. 308–310), testing his reported 6.5 percentage point (SE = 3.2) phone-call effect, one-to-one vs. one-to-five matching, matching with vs. without replacement, actual vs. bootstrap samples, household-size subgroup estimates, and ITT/untreated diagnostic comparisons, and additionally tests Imai's 6.5 percentage point claim and matching estimator in a new 2002 Iowa/Michigan field experiment (pp. 303–304, 310). The only shipped row (input_row_index 46, Gerber & Green 2000, DOI 10.2307/2585837) represents Gerber and Green's own 1998 New Haven experiment (target_index 0), not Imai (2005)'s separate reanalysis paper; earlier unpublished versions (Imai 2002 manuscript and Imai 2003 dissertation) are superseded by the published 2005 APSR article.

decisions.location: Study 2 Introduction, p. 613 (see also Abstract, p. 603; Introduction, pp. 604–605; General Discussion, p. 618)
decisions.quote:
Study 2 served as an extension of Shuler and
Carroll (2019). The purpose of Study 2 was to
examine the effects of supervisor feedback on
therapists’ guided-compliance integrity with a
child with ASD.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. Reading the full text establishes that Carroll, Preas, and Paden (2022) explicitly designed Study 1 as a direct replication of Shuler and Carroll (2019) (target_index 0, already represented by shipped row input_row_index 800, DOI 10.1007/s40617-018-00314-5, published online in 2018 and in print in 2019) and Study 2 as a novel extension of Shuler and Carroll (2019) testing whether therapists with no prior training in guided compliance acquire guided-compliance integrity when given feedback alone from the VMVO-trained supervisors from Study 1. Parsons and Reid (1995) evaluated an intensive 8-hour didactic, role-play, and in-vivo supervisor training package for maintaining previously trained staff teaching skills in an adult residential facility; the source cites Parsons and Reid (1995) as background that Shuler and Carroll (2019) extended (p. 604), for feedback step definitions/mastery criteria (pp. 606, 619), and in a single General Discussion sentence noting that Study 2 extends previous studies (p. 618). Under the codebook rules on background/extension and replication chains, Parsons and Reid (1995) is positively established background/extension rather than a directly retested original target.

decisions.location: Discussion, lines 494–498 (see also Results, lines 292–307, and Discussion, lines 387–403)
decisions.quote:
In sum, we could not replicate findings of our previous EWAS approach
21
and studies by others
20
.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. In an independent sample of 189 female patients with anorexia nervosa and 67 healthy-lean controls, Rajcsanyi et al. (2025) empirically test DNA methylation across 15 CpG sites at the NR1H3 locus using two-sided robust linear regression (Results, lines 292–307; Methods, line 542) and explicitly evaluate both the hypomethylation finding of their own prior EWAS (Kesselmeier et al. 2018/2016, reference 21, target_index 0) and the opposite hypermethylation finding reported by Booij et al. (2015, reference 20, target_index 1), concluding in the Discussion that 'we were unable to replicate methylation differences at NR1H3 , regardless of the methylation direction previously reported 20 , 21' (lines 397–403) and 'could not replicate findings of our previous EWAS approach 21 and studies by others 20' (lines 494–498). Shipped row 1217 (Kesselmeier et al. 2016/2018, DOI 10.1080/15622975.2016.1190033) is a separate study by a different research group reporting opposite methylation direction at NR1H3, so Booij et al. (2015) (DOI 10.1002/eat.22374) is a genuinely absent original target.

decisions.location: Discussion, p. 14 (see also Results, p. 9, and References, p. 17)
decisions.quote:
The current study had three main objectives: (a) to replicate the behavioral findings of Dumontheil
and colleagues (2010), (b) to assess the role of inhibitory control in this task across age groups, and (c)
to compare the time course of information processing among children, adolescents, and adults
through eye-tracking in order to determine in what ways the deployment of ToM differs across age
groups.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. Symeonidou et al. (2015) explicitly set out to replicate and empirically re-test the developmental behavioral findings of Dumontheil, Apperly, and Blakemore (2010) on the computerized Director vs. No-Director perspective-taking task in a new sample of children, adolescents, and adults (N = 65), comparing accuracy and reaction times across age groups and conditions (Results, p. 9; Discussion, p. 14). The sole shipped row (input_row_index 2150, Cacchione & Call 2010, DOI 10.1111/j.1467-7687.2009.00881.x, 'Intuitions about gravity and solidity in great apes: the tubes task') is a completely unrelated article published in the same volume of Developmental Science (resulting from a one-digit DOI mismatch in the shipped dataset) and is never cited in the source paper. Dumontheil et al. (2010) is verified in the reference list (p. 17, without a printed DOI) and is genuinely absent from the shipped rows.

decisions.quote: This study examines career planning programs and career services offices at colleges and universities in the United States as viewed by senior student affairs officers (SSAOs). Findings from a 1979 study of career services offices (CSOs) were compared to the current findings.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. The blind coder had access only to the four-line abstract of Vinson, Reardon, and Bertoch (2014) ('Career Services at Colleges and Universities: A 30-Year Replication Study'), which states that findings from a 1979 study of career services offices at colleges and universities were compared to the current findings without printing the full citation in the abstract. Shipped row input_row_index 382 (Reardon, Zunker, & Dyal 1979, 'The Status of Career Planning Programs and Career Centers in Colleges and Universities', DOI 10.1002/j.2164-585x.1979.tb00097.x, co-authored by Robert C. Reardon, who is also second author of the 2014 replication study) is the exact 1979 study described in target_index 0, so the target is already represented in the shipped dataset.

decisions.location: Introduction, p. 6 (see also Title, p. 1; Abstract, p. 2; Hypotheses 1 and 3, p. 8; References, p. 26)
decisions.quote:
We sought to conceptually replicate two studies of the role of linguistic style in

predicting war attitudes and behaviors, Abe (2012) and Matsumoto and Hwang (2013), in

the U.S. Congressional context.
decisions.reason: Jordan, Buchanan, and Padfield explicitly frame their paper in the title, abstract, introduction, and hypotheses as a conceptual replication of both Abe (2012) and Matsumoto and Hwang (2013), stating that their work is 'a more direct replication of Matsumoto and Hwang (2013) with the only substantive difference being the sample itself and the outcome measure' (p. 7) and empirically testing Matsumoto and Hwang (2013)'s findings via Hypothesis 1 (greater external focus / third-person pronouns among war supporters) and Hypothesis 3 (lower cognitive complexity among war supporters) across five U.S. congressional speech datasets (Studies 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, and 3). The sole shipped row (input_row_index 2365, Abe 2012, DOI 10.1177/0261927x12438532) represents target_index 0, a distinct study of online forum posts by a different author, whereas Matsumoto and Hwang (2013) (verified in the reference list, p. 26, with DOI 10.1177/0261927X12460666; occasionally mis-cited in the Discussion as the review article Matsumoto, Frank, & Hwang 2015) is a separate original study of political leaders' speeches and is genuinely absent from the shipped rows.
